line_1.speaker: Serjeant Halbrek
line_1.text: Because the alternative is deciding which eleven to leave out, and I am not owed that decision. Nobody offered me it.

line_2.speaker: Serjeant Halbrek
line_2.text: Nobody descends. I countersigned it. Then I descended, because somebody had to be the exception, and exceptions are what serjeants are for.

line_3.speaker: Serjeant Halbrek
line_3.text: Guard pattern. Short, ugly, meant for a doorway you cannot afford to lose. Aldric has the drawing now. He will complain about it and then make it well.

gated.speaker: Serjeant Halbrek
gated.text: You have been down past the Vault. Then you have seen the crates. We loaded those. We were told they were grain.

start.speaker: Serjeant Halbrek
start.text: Serjeant Halbrek has taken a corner of the tower and made it look lived in, which is more than the tower has managed on its own.

choices.text: I have been in the Vault.

halbrek_arc.speaker: Halbrek
halbrek_arc.text: Forty-one at muster. Thirty at supper. I called all forty-one for eleven years because stopping would have been a decision, and I was not given the authority to make it. You may consider the board open.
